newsitem.title: UK: Psion continues fall, promises turnaround.
newsitem.headline: Psion continues fall, promises turnaround.

text.p: The share price of British hand-held computers firm Psion Plc continued its downward trend on Monday by shedding nearly a pound, even as it promised a turnaround in its performance based on launch of its new Series 5 computer.

Psion was down 97-1/2 pence at 407 1/2p at about 0920 GMT, after the company said the strength of the sterling combined with a slowdown of its Series 3 sales in May and June would affect its performance until the Series 5 was established.

The company's chairman David Potter said on Monday that it was initially shifting 10,000 units of the new 32-bit computer each month and gradually hopes to sell nearly 40,000 each month by September/October.

Potter told a news conference that the new computer, which has compatibility with Microsoft office products, Lotus Smartsuite and Corel/Wordperfect was expected to comprise nearly 40 to 50 percent of Psion's annual turnover by next year.
He said initial reviews of Series 5 and orders were "good" and "encouraging".
"Investors need to examine the totality of what we are doing. They need to examine the very major step that we are taking today," he said.
Psion will sell its Series 5 to over 50 countries in eight language variants. The company will also continue to make and market its Series 3 and Siena products.
